dataset_family: Duke University iMIND / Eye Multimodal Imaging in Neurodegenerative Disease Study (EMINDS), Duke IRB Pro00082598 (= NCT03233646, linked on p.2 of P-363). MCI from the Duke Memory Clinic; controls from the community, Duke clinics and the Duke Alzheimer's Disease Prevention Registry. This is the same dataset family as candidate P-163 and as P-363.
method_family: Ultra-widefield scanning-laser-ophthalmoscope fundus imaging (Optos, non-mydriatic) with semi-automated vessel morphometry (VAMPIRE-UWF 2.0): width gradient and intercept, tortuosity, fractal dimension, red-channel choroidal vascular density. Group comparison by GEE adjusted for age and sex; no classifier.
what_it_shows: Joseph et al. 2024, Ophthalmology Science. On UWF fundus images (131 eyes of 82 MCI vs 230 eyes of 133 CN, age-similar), MCI had smaller retinal artery and vein width intercepts (P < 0.001; P = 0.017) and less negative width gradients (P < 0.001; P = 0.027). Large-vessel choroidal vascular density was higher (P = 0.025). Tortuosity and fractal dimension did not differ. These are group associations only, uncorrected for multiple comparisons, with no diagnostic accuracy.
why: PDF identity confirmed: title, authors (Joseph, Haystead, Robbins, Threlfall, MacGillivray, Stinnett, Grewal, Fekrat) and DOI 10.1016/j.xops.2024.100480 match the block. I read the whole extract through the references. STATED FORM, partly: its own GEE comparison supports retinal (vascular) structure as a biomarker direction for MCI. It reports no detection performance and does not test scalability. Imaging is non-mydriatic, which is relevant to feasibility, but 118 of 480 eyes (25%) were excluded for image quality, which cuts against easy deployment. NARROWED FORM, yes, on the headline: a preliminary, single-centre association of retinal imaging (fundus, here UWF-SLO) with MCI, age-similar (70.7 vs 70.4, P = 0.155) and adjusted for age and sex with fellow-eye correlation handled. It shows association, not discrimination, so the sub-clause 'discriminated MCI' does not describe it. CAVEATS: exploratory, with no multiple-comparison correction (authors, p.8); several effects are modest (P = 0.017 to 0.027); sex imbalance (48.8% vs 22.6% male, adjusted); clinical MCI without biomarkers; not all controls were evaluated by neurologists (p.8); the red-channel choroidal binarisation is unvalidated (p.8); Optos loaned the device and part-funded the work (p.9). INDEPENDENCE, which decides its value here: it comes from the same Duke protocol as candidate P-163. P-363 prints NCT03233646 and IRB Pro00082598 together (p.2). P-163 prints NCT03233646 and P-1317 prints Pro00082598, and all three share Robbins, Grewal and Fekrat. It therefore adds no independent dataset family beyond P-163; at most one Duke paper can count. It is independent of the current supporters P-5, P-952, P-966 and P-105. Not a preprint: peer-reviewed Ophthalmology Science article. The Elsevier extract renders minus signs as 'e' in Table 2 (e.g. 'e2.46'); I read them as negative gradients, which is consistent with the text.

quotes.quote: One hundred thirty-one eyes of 82 MCI patients and 230 eyes of 133 cognitively normal participants from the Eye Multimodal Imaging in Neurodegenerative Disease Study.
Duke Health Institutional Review Board (Pro00082598) approval was obtained.
Study participants > 50 years of age were enrolled from the Duke Memory Clinic. Individuals with a clinical diagnosis of MCI were diagnosed by Duke neurologists specializing in memory disorders

Generalized estimating equations, adjusted for age and sex, were then used to compare the imaging parameters between groups while accounting for the correlation between 2 eyes within the same study participant.

We imaged 176 eyes from 88 MCI patients and 304 eyes from 152 control participants. Of these, 45 MCI eyes and 73 control eyes were excluded because of poor image quality/significant image artifact after manual review.
Average arterial and venous width gradients were less negative, representing decreased rates of vessel thinning, among individuals with MCI compared with that of controls (P < 0.001; P = 0.027).
Average retinal arterial and venous width intercepts were smaller, representing thinner vessels, among individuals with MCI compared with controls (P < 0.001; P = 0.017).
Large vessel choroidal vascular density was higher, indicating increased choroidal vascular density, in individuals with MCI compared with that of controls (P = 0.025).
Because of the exploratory nature of this study, correction for multiple associations was not performed. As such, there may be an increased risk of type 1 error in this study.
